raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #57929

**What/Why:** Non-streaming `/v1/completions/derender` returned `prompt_logprobs: null` — `OnlineDerenderer._derender_completion` built each choice without the field, discarding data the engine had already computed. The chat derender path and direct `/v1/completions` already pass it through.

**How:** One line in `vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py` — attach `gen.prompt_logprobs` to every choice of that response (per-prompt semantics identical to the direct endpoint), plus regression test 

**Updated:** Chat fills `prompt_logprobs` inside `_derender_chat`, in the same background call that decodes the text 

`test_derender_completion_prompt_logprobs_passthrough` in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py` (fails on unfixed code, passes after).


**Tests:** `pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py` → 37/37 passed locally; pre-commit clean; GPU parity suite left to CI. Not model-affecting (frontend response assembly only).

**AI Assistance** 
Co-Authored-By: ZCode GLM 5.3 / Claude

nodes.body: Thanks @akshay-babbar for the update. LGTM.

**Nothing blocking.** The comments below are optional suggestions. There is no need to push a fix for them before merging.

**Additional findings** (outside the current diff — GitHub can't attach inline comments there):

- 🟡 `vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py` — Derender callers can now make the server tokenizer-decode every id in caller-supplied `prompt_logprobs`, and nothing caps how many entries each position holds. `_validate_derender_bounds` caps `top_logprobs` per choice entry at `max_logprobs`. For `prompt_logprobs` it checks only the outer length against `max_model_len`, but `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` (online_derenderer.py:1016) decodes every entry whose `decoded_token` is None. Fix: reject any `prompt_logprobs` position whose dict has more than `max_logprobs + 1` entries, on both the chat and completion paths. Also deduplicate `missing` before `convert_ids_list_to_tokens`.

  <details><summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

  A client POSTs to /v1/chat/completions/derender or /v1/completions/derender. Its generate_response.prompt_logprobs has up to max_model_len positions, each a dict with thousands of token ids and decoded_token=null. `_validate_derender_bounds` (serving.py:111-115) checks only `len(gen.prompt_logprobs) > max_model_len`. It never checks per-position dict size, though it does check `len(entry.top_logprobs) > max_logprobs` for choice logprobs at serving.py:98-108. `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` (online_derenderer.py:1016-1027) then decodes every id with `convert_ids_list_to_tokens`, including repeats, because `missing` is not deduplicated. On the base branch, chat passed `gen.prompt_logprobs` through without decoding and completion dropped it, so the server did no work proportional to that structure.

  **Verification:** Trigger: prompt_logprobs positions holding large dicts with decoded_token=null. `_validate_derender_bounds` checks only the outer length (serving.py:111-116). The new `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` (online_derenderer.py:1003-1044) collects every tid with `lp.decoded_token is None` and runs `convert_ids_list_to_tokens`. On the base, prompt_logprobs were passed through on chat and dropped on completions.

  </details>

<!-- bhrv:ff66fd202082ed9b -->

🟡 (optional) Derender requests whose prompt_logprobs contain a token id with no vocab entry, or a negative one, now fail with a 500; the base branch passed them through. `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` hands every key with `decoded_token=None` to `convert_ids_list_to_tokens`, and nothing validates those keys. Fix: before decoding, check every prompt_logprobs key the same way `choice.token_ids` is checked (non-negative, inside the vocab), returning a 400. Otherwise map an id with no vocab entry to "", as `resolve_token_id_placeholder` already does.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

A client POSTs to /v1/chat/completions/derender or /v1/completions/derender. Its generate_response.prompt_logprobs has a dict key that is out of vocab or negative, with decoded_token null. protocol.py:443 types the field as `list[dict[int, Logprob] | None]` with no key validation. At online_derenderer.py:1025, `convert_ids_list_to_tokens` calls `tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens`, which returns None for unknown ids. `_restore_leading_spaces` then runs `for ch in None` and raises TypeError on SentencePiece-marker tokenizers. HF fast `decode([-1])` raises OverflowError. The chat handler at serving.py:173 catches only ValueError, and the completion call at serving.py:235 has no handler at all, so the client gets a 500. On the base branch prompt_logprobs went through untouched and these requests succeeded.

**Verification:** `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` (online_derenderer.py ~1015-1025) collects every key whose `decoded_token is None` and calls `convert_ids_list_to_tokens(tokenizer, missing)`. Nothing validates those keys first. The chat path catches only `ValueError` (serving.py:172). Before this change, either request got a 200. Now the request fails with an unhandled exception, which surfaces as a 500.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:nit -->

nodes.body:
🟡 (optional) Derender callers whose router re-serializes `prompt_logprobs` with sorted or unordered map keys can get wrong `decoded_token` text for multi-byte (U+FFFD) prompt tokens. On base those fields stayed null. `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` takes the correction context from `next(iter(entry))`, the first JSON key of each position. That is only the prompt token if JSON object key order survives every hop. Fix: take the context from the real prompt ids, such as `gen.prompt_token_ids[i]` or a full-length caller `prompt_token_ids`, when their length matches `prompt_logprobs`. Fall back to key order only when neither is available.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is a caller of /v1/chat/completions/derender or /v1/completions/derender whose generate_response passed through a component that does not keep JSON object key order. The generate server (token_in_token_out/serving.py:469) emits the prompt token first, but JSON objects are unordered by spec and the derender request is caller-supplied. In `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` (online_derenderer.py:1043), `context_token_ids.append(next(iter(entry)))` then records an arbitrary top-k id, such as the smallest id, as the earlier prompt token. For any missing decoded_token that ends in U+FFFD, `_correct_decoded_token` (line 1038) decodes it against these wrong ids. That returns garbage or "" rather than what `vllm serve` returns. On base, decoded_token stayed null, so callers could tell it was missing; now it is wrong without any warning.

**Verification:** The field is client-supplied data: `GenerateResponseBase.prompt_logprobs` (token_in_token_out/protocol.py:443) arrives in the derender request body, and pydantic accepts any key order. Nothing checks that the first key is the prompt token. The base branch returned null for these fields, so the result changes from missing to silently wrong.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:nit -->

@@ -993,6 +1000,50 @@ def _correct_decoded_token(
     return ""
 
 
+def _resolve_prompt_logprobs(
+    prompt_logprobs: PromptLogprobs | None, tokenizer: TokenizerLike
+) -> PromptLogprobs | None:
+    """Fill missing ``decoded_token`` values in prompt logprobs.
+
+    A ``--tokens-only`` generate server has no tokenizer, so it returns
+    ``decoded_token=None``. Mirrors LogprobsProcessor._update_prompt_logprobs
+    in v1/engine/logprobs.py: decode each token id, then fix U+FFFD using the
+    preceding prompt tokens (the first entry of each earlier position).
+    """
+    if prompt_logprobs is None:
+        return None
+
+    missing = [
+        tid
+        for entry in prompt_logprobs
+        if entry is not None
+        for tid, lp in entry.items()
+        if lp.decoded_token is None
+    ]
+    if not missing:
+        return prompt_logprobs
+    decoded = dict(zip(missing, convert_ids_list_to_tokens(tokenizer, missing)))
+
+    resolved: PromptLogprobs = []
+    context_token_ids: list[int] = []
+    for entry in prompt_logprobs:
+        if not entry:
+            resolved.append(entry)
+            continue
+        new_entry: dict[int, Logprob] = {}
+        for tid, lp in entry.items():
+            if lp.decoded_token is None:
+                text = decoded[tid]
+                if text.endswith("\ufffd"):
+                    text = _correct_decoded_token(tid, context_token_ids, tokenizer)
+                lp = Logprob(lp.logprob, lp.rank, text)
+            new_entry[tid] = lp
+        resolved.append(new_entry)
+        # The prompt token is always inserted first by the engine.
+        context_token_ids.append(next(iter(entry)))

+async def test_derender_completion_prompt_logprobs_passthrough(client):
+    """Each GenerateResponse's prompt_logprobs reaches that prompt's choices.
+
+    Regression test: /v1/completions/derender used to drop the prompt
+    logprobs the engine had already computed and returned, while the direct
+    /v1/completions endpoint attaches them to every choice of the prompt.
+    """
+    gr1 = await _render_completion(client, "Hello")
+    gr2 = await _render_completion(client, "World")
+    tok = get_tokenizer(MODEL_NAME)
+    # A --tokens-only generate server has no tokenizer: decoded_token is null.
+    plp1 = [None, {str(gr1["token_ids"][0]): {"logprob": -0.5, "rank": 1}}]
+    plp2 = [None, {str(gr2["token_ids"][0]): {"logprob": -0.25, "rank": 2}}]

+        "/v1/completions/derender",
+        json={
+            "model": MODEL_NAME,
+            "generate_responses": [
+                _make_completion_generate_response(
+                    gr1["token_ids"][:3], gr1["request_id"], prompt_logprobs=plp1
+                ),
+                _make_completion_generate_response(
+                    gr2["token_ids"][:3], gr2["request_id"], prompt_logprobs=plp2
+                ),
+            ],
+        },
+    )
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    choices = response.json()["choices"]

+        tid = gr["token_ids"][0]
+        (text,) = convert_ids_list_to_tokens(tok, [tid])
+        entry = choice["prompt_logprobs"][1][str(tid)]
+        assert plp[1] is not None
+        assert choice["prompt_logprobs"][0] is None
+        assert entry["decoded_token"] == text
+        assert entry["logprob"] == plp[1][str(tid)]["logprob"]
+        assert entry["rank"] == plp[1][str(tid)]["rank"]
+
+

+    )

🟡 (optional) Derender requests whose prompt_logprobs contain a token id with no vocab entry, or a negative one, now fail with a 500; the base branch passed them through. `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` hands every key with `decoded_token=None` to `convert_ids_list_to_tokens`, and nothing validates those keys. Fix: before decoding, check every prompt_logprobs key the same way `choice.token_ids` is checked (non-negative, inside the vocab), returning a 400. Otherwise map an id with no vocab entry to "", as `resolve_token_id_placeholder` already does.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

A client POSTs to /v1/chat/completions/derender or /v1/completions/derender. Its generate_response.prompt_logprobs has a dict key that is out of vocab or negative, with decoded_token null. protocol.py:443 types the field as `list[dict[int, Logprob] | None]` with no key validation. At online_derenderer.py:1025, `convert_ids_list_to_tokens` calls `tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens`, which returns None for unknown ids. `_restore_leading_spaces` then runs `for ch in None` and raises TypeError on SentencePiece-marker tokenizers. HF fast `decode([-1])` raises OverflowError. The chat handler at serving.py:173 catches only ValueError, and the completion call at serving.py:235 has no handler at all, so the client gets a 500. On the base branch prompt_logprobs went through untouched and these requests succeeded.

**Verification:** `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` (online_derenderer.py ~1015-1025) collects every key whose `decoded_token is None` and calls `convert_ids_list_to_tokens(tokenizer, missing)`. Nothing validates those keys first. The chat path catches only `ValueError` (serving.py:172). Before this change, either request got a 200. Now the request fails with an unhandled exception, which surfaces as a 500.

</details>

🟡 (optional) Derender callers whose router re-serializes `prompt_logprobs` with sorted or unordered map keys can get wrong `decoded_token` text for multi-byte (U+FFFD) prompt tokens. On base those fields stayed null. `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` takes the correction context from `next(iter(entry))`, the first JSON key of each position. That is only the prompt token if JSON object key order survives every hop. Fix: take the context from the real prompt ids, such as `gen.prompt_token_ids[i]` or a full-length caller `prompt_token_ids`, when their length matches `prompt_logprobs`. Fall back to key order only when neither is available.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is a caller of /v1/chat/completions/derender or /v1/completions/derender whose generate_response passed through a component that does not keep JSON object key order. The generate server (token_in_token_out/serving.py:469) emits the prompt token first, but JSON objects are unordered by spec and the derender request is caller-supplied. In `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` (online_derenderer.py:1043), `context_token_ids.append(next(iter(entry)))` then records an arbitrary top-k id, such as the smallest id, as the earlier prompt token. For any missing decoded_token that ends in U+FFFD, `_correct_decoded_token` (line 1038) decodes it against these wrong ids. That returns garbage or "" rather than what `vllm serve` returns. On base, decoded_token stayed null, so callers could tell it was missing; now it is wrong without any warning.

**Verification:** The field is client-supplied data: `GenerateResponseBase.prompt_logprobs` (token_in_token_out/protocol.py:443) arrives in the derender request body, and pydantic accepts any key order. Nothing checks that the first key is the prompt token. The base branch returned null for these fields, so the result changes from missing to silently wrong.

</details>

Thanks @akshay-babbar for pushing the fix.

This fixes the `null` but with a `--tokens-only` generate server there's no tokenizer, so every `decoded_token` comes through as `None` (chat derender has the same problem). The test hand writes `decoded_token: "H"`, so it doesn't catch that. Derender should fill them in the way the engine does in `_update_prompt_logprobs`. It's the same fix as #59241.

Small nit, can you update the PR description. You can also state that it fixes chat derender as well.

**Nothing blocking.** The comments below are optional suggestions. There is no need to push a fix for them before merging.

**Additional findings** (outside the current diff — GitHub can't attach inline comments there):

- 🟡 `vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py` — Derender callers can now make the server tokenizer-decode every id in caller-supplied `prompt_logprobs`, and nothing caps how many entries each position holds. `_validate_derender_bounds` caps `top_logprobs` per choice entry at `max_logprobs`. For `prompt_logprobs` it checks only the outer length against `max_model_len`, but `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` (online_derenderer.py:1016) decodes every entry whose `decoded_token` is None. Fix: reject any `prompt_logprobs` position whose dict has more than `max_logprobs + 1` entries, on both the chat and completion paths. Also deduplicate `missing` before `convert_ids_list_to_tokens`.

  <details><summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

  A client POSTs to /v1/chat/completions/derender or /v1/completions/derender. Its generate_response.prompt_logprobs has up to max_model_len positions, each a dict with thousands of token ids and decoded_token=null. `_validate_derender_bounds` (serving.py:111-115) checks only `len(gen.prompt_logprobs) > max_model_len`. It never checks per-position dict size, though it does check `len(entry.top_logprobs) > max_logprobs` for choice logprobs at serving.py:98-108. `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` (online_derenderer.py:1016-1027) then decodes every id with `convert_ids_list_to_tokens`, including repeats, because `missing` is not deduplicated. On the base branch, chat passed `gen.prompt_logprobs` through without decoding and completion dropped it, so the server did no work proportional to that structure.

  **Verification:** Trigger: prompt_logprobs positions holding large dicts with decoded_token=null. `_validate_derender_bounds` checks only the outer length (serving.py:111-116). The new `_resolve_prompt_logprobs` (online_derenderer.py:1003-1044) collects every tid with `lp.decoded_token is None` and runs `convert_ids_list_to_tokens`. On the base, prompt_logprobs were passed through on chat and dropped on completions.

  </details>
